title: Vibhaṅga Library
tagline: The second book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka — the Book of Analysis — its text and commentaries, one section per page, linked paragraph by paragraph.

books.title: The Book of Analysis (Vibhaṅga)
books.author: U Thiṭṭila
books.edition: PTS Translation Series 39, 1969; electronic edition 2010 (CC BY-NC 3.0)
books.by: Translated from the Pāḷi of the Burmese Chaṭṭhasaṅgīti edition by Paṭhamakyaw Ashin Thiṭṭila (Seṭṭhila), Aggamahāpaṇḍita · Pali Text Society
books.blurb: The Vibhaṅga in English, translated from the same Sixth Council text that is on the Pāli shelf, paragraph by paragraph.
books.note: The translation, one part per vibhaṅga as in the Pāli reader (so far the Analysis of the Aggregates to the Analysis of the Path Constituents, §1–507; the rest is being added). Each § is the Sixth Council paragraph and links to the same paragraph in the Pāli and the commentaries. The margin gives the pages of the printed translation and, marked P, of the PTS Pāli edition (Rhys Davids 1904), which Thiṭṭila prints in square brackets. The small lines under a paragraph are his notes (P¹ = see para. …).
books.toc_foot: The Book of Analysis ({{NPARA}} numbered paragraphs, the Sixth Council numbers).
books.source: Source: U Thiṭṭila, The Book of Analysis (Vibhaṅga), Pali Text Society Translation Series 39 (1969; electronic edition, Bristol 2010), published by the Pali Text Society under the Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial 3.0 licence. The text is taken from the PDF as it is; the line-end hyphens are resolved, and the pages are kept as anchors.
books.desc: U Thiṭṭila’s Book of Analysis, the Vibhaṅga in English, linked paragraph by paragraph to the Pāli and its commentaries.
howto: Type a number in § (1–1044): the Sixth Council numbers, as in the Pāli.
The chips beside a § open the same paragraph in the Pāli and the commentaries.
books.drawer_hint: The text has no index of its own.

books.title: Vibhaṅgapāḷi
books.short: Vibhaṅga in the Sixth Council Pāḷi
books.author: Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana
books.edition: Sixth Council edition (Yangon, 1954–56), VRI digital text
books.by: Abhidhammapiṭaka, Vibhaṅgapāḷi · the text of the Sixth Buddhist Council (Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana), Yangon · digital edition of the Vipassana Research Institute
books.blurb: The Book of Analysis itself: eighteen vibhaṅgas, from the aggregates to the heart of the Dhamma, most of them analysed three ways — by the suttas, by the Abhidhamma, and by questions on the mātikā.
books.note: The whole text, one part per vibhaṅga (the longest in two or three): the Khandha-, Āyatana-, Dhātu-, Sacca-, Indriya-, Paṭiccasamuppāda-, Satipaṭṭhāna-, Sammappadhāna-, Iddhipāda-, Bojjhaṅga-, Maggaṅga-, Jhāna-, Appamaññā-, Sikkhāpada-, Paṭisambhidā-, Ñāṇa-, Khuddakavatthu- and Dhammahadaya-vibhaṅga (§1–1044). Each § links to the commentary and sub-commentaries on it; the margin gives the pages of the Myanmar edition and, marked P, of the PTS edition (Rhys Davids 1904); the edition’s variant readings are notes.
books.toc_foot: The eighteen vibhaṅgas ({{NPARA}} numbered paragraphs), in the Sixth Council text.
books.source: Source: the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana (Sixth Council) text of the Vibhaṅga as published in digital form by the Vipassana Research Institute (romn/abh02m.mul.xml, github.com/VipassanaTech/tipitaka-xml). The text is unchanged; its paragraph numbers, the pages of the Myanmar edition and, marked P, of the PTS edition, and the variant readings are as in the file.
books.desc: The Vibhaṅga in the Pāli of the Sixth Council edition, with its paragraph numbers, page numbers and variant readings, linked to its commentaries.
howto: Type in Search (or press /). Accents are optional: rupa finds rūpa.
The small chips beside a § open the Sammohavinodanī, the Mūlaṭīkā and the Anuṭīkā on the same paragraph.
books.drawer_hint: The text has no index of its own.

books.title: Sammohavinodanī
books.author: Buddhaghosa
books.edition: Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā, Sixth Council edition, VRI digital text
books.by: Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā (Sammohavinodanī nāma), ascribed to Buddhaghosa (5th century) · the text of the Sixth Buddhist Council (Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana), Yangon · digital edition of the Vipassana Research Institute
books.blurb: “The Dispeller of Delusion”: the commentary on the Vibhaṅga, in the Pāli of the Sixth Council edition, vibhaṅga by vibhaṅga — with its long treatments of dependent origination, the foundations of mindfulness and jhāna.
books.note: The whole commentary, one part per vibhaṅga (the longest cut at their sections). Each numbered paragraph explains the Vibhaṅga paragraph with the same number, and links to it in the Pāli text and to the sub-commentaries on it; those link back. The words explained are in bold, as in the edition. The margin gives the pages of the Myanmar edition and, marked P, of the PTS edition (A. P. Buddhadatta 1923), which Ñāṇamoli’s translation, The Dispeller of Delusion, gives in its margin.
books.toc_foot: The eighteen vibhaṅgas ({{NPARA}} numbered paragraphs, by the paragraph of the Vibhaṅga they explain).
books.source: Source: the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana (Sixth Council) text of the Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā (Sammohavinodanī) as published in digital form by the Vipassana Research Institute (romn/abh02a.att.xml, github.com/VipassanaTech/tipitaka-xml). The text is unchanged; its paragraph numbers, the pages of the Myanmar edition and, marked P, of the PTS edition, and the variant readings are as in the file.
books.desc: The Sammohavinodanī, the commentary on the Vibhaṅga, in the Sixth Council Pāli, linked paragraph by paragraph to the text.
howto: Type in Search (or press /). Accents are optional: rupa finds rūpa.
Go to the commentary on a paragraph
Type the number of the Vibhaṅga paragraph in § (1–1044); not every paragraph has its own comment.
The chips beside a § open that paragraph in the Pāli text and the sub-commentaries on it.

books.drawer_hint: The text has no index of its own.

books.blurb: Ānanda’s sub-commentary, which explains the Sammohavinodanī in its turn, in the Pāli of the Sixth Council edition.
books.note: The whole sub-commentary, one part per vibhaṅga. Its numbered paragraphs follow the Vibhaṅga paragraph that the Sammohavinodanī explains, and link to that paragraph in the commentary, the Pāli text and the Anuṭīkā. The words explained are in bold.

The text is unchanged; its paragraph numbers, the pages of the Myanmar edition and, marked P, of the PTS edition, and the variant readings are as in the file.
books.desc: Ānanda’s Mūlaṭīkā on the Sammohavinodanī, in the Sixth Council Pāli, linked to the commentary and the text by paragraph.
